title: Integral adic trace formula for Frobenius coefficient morphisms
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ and the coefficient
conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with
$A_n=A_{E,n}$. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme,
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, let $K_\bullet$ be a normalized $A_\bullet$-system on
$X$ and $\psi_\bullet$ a compatible system of Frobenius coefficient
morphisms on it, in the sense of [prop-trf-adic-coefficient-morphism-systems],
with $P_n$, $P_{\bar y,n}$, $P_{\mathcal O}$, $P_{\bar y,\mathcal O}$ as
there; no invertibility of the $\psi_n$ is assumed. At every finite level
$n$ assume the hypotheses of [thm-trf-coefficient-morphism-trace-formula]
for $(K_n,\psi_n)$: an explicit etale-origin witness for $K_n$
([def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]) and the exceptional-adjoint
admissibility of [def-trf-admissibility] for the graph correspondences and
fixed-point base changes on a chosen compactification defined over $k_0$.

1. For every $m\geq1$,
$$
\boxed{\,
\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}\bigl(F_{c,m}(\psi_\bullet)\mid P_{\mathcal O}\bigr)
=\sum_{y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})}
\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}\bigl(\psi_{\bullet,m,\bar y}\mid P_{\bar y,\mathcal O}\bigr)
\,}
$$
in $\mathcal O_E$; that is, $\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}(V_m)=\sum_y
\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}(V_{y,m})$ for any lifts $V_m$ of
$(F_{c,m}(\psi_n))_n$ and $V_{y,m}$ of $(\psi_{n,m,\bar y})_n$.
1. *Lattice form.* Let $K_{\mathcal O}$, $\varphi_E=\varpi^{-N}u$, $\psi_n=u_n\circ\kappa_{K_n}$,
$U_m$ and $U_{y,m}$ be as in [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model]
(so $K_\bullet$ is the reduction tower of $K_{\mathcal O}$), and assume the
finite-level hypotheses above. Then for every $m\geq1$
$$
\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}\bigl(U_m\mid R\Gamma_c(X,K_{\mathcal O})\bigr)
=\sum_{y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})}
\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}\bigl(U_{y,m}\mid K_{\mathcal O,\bar y}\bigr)
\quad\text{in }\mathcal O_E .
$$

proof.text: Fix $m\geq1$ and put $Y_m=X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$. This set is finite by clause (1) of [lem-weil-point-counts-finite], applied to the finite-type $k_0$-scheme $X_0$ and the finite extension $\mathbf F_{q^m}/k_0$. It depends on $X_0$ and $m$, not on the coefficient level $n$. By [prop-trf-adic-coefficient-morphism-systems], items (1)–(3), the complexes $P_n,P_{\bar y,n}$ are perfect, the two operator families $(F_{c,m}(\psi_n))_n$ and $(\psi_{n,m,\bar y})_n$ are compatible, and their integral realizations are bounded finite-free complexes admitting lifts of these families. Choose any such lifts $V_m$ and $V_{y,m}$ for $y\in Y_m$. No strict Weil structure or invertibility of $\psi_n$ is required by this proposition.

source.place: (1), existence of lifts and finiteness of the common index set

proof.text:
For each $n\geq1$, apply [thm-trf-coefficient-morphism-trace-formula] with coefficient ring $A_n$, complex $K_n$ and coefficient morphism $\psi_n$. The common finite-field datum and the separated finite-type scheme are those of the hypotheses; $K_n\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$ follows from the assumed normalized system, and the explicit etale-origin witness and the graph/fixed-point exceptional-adjoint admissibility on the compactification over $k_0$ are assumed at this level. The theorem does not assume invertibility. Its stalk endomorphism is $(\psi_{n,m})_{\bar y}\circ\iota_{K_n}$, exactly the normalization in the operator-compatibility clause of [prop-trf-adic-coefficient-morphism-systems]. Consequently
$$a_n:=\operatorname{tr}_{A_n}(F_{c,m}(\psi_n)\mid P_n)=\sum_{y\in Y_m}\operatorname{tr}_{A_n}(\psi_{n,m,\bar y}\mid P_{\bar y,n})=:\sum_{y\in Y_m}b_{y,n}.$$

source.place: (1), application of the finite-level trace identity

proof.text: Put $a=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}(V_m\mid P_{\mathcal O})$ and $b_y=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}(V_{y,m}\mid P_{\bar y,\mathcal O})$. Item (4) of [prop-trf-adic-coefficient-morphism-systems], applied to these arbitrary lifts, gives $\rho_n(a)=a_n$ and $\rho_n(b_y)=b_{y,n}$, where $\rho_n:\mathcal O_E\to A_n$ is reduction. It also identifies these integral traces with the corresponding elements of $\varprojlim_n A_n=\mathcal O_E$, independently of the lifts. Thus the notation for the traces in clause (1) is defined even when the operators are not invertible.

source.place: (1), traces of lifts and their finite reductions

proof.text:
Since $Y_m$ is finite by step 1, additivity of the quotient ring homomorphism $\rho_n$ gives
$$\rho_n\Bigl(a-\sum_{y\in Y_m}b_y\Bigr)=a_n-\sum_{y\in Y_m}b_{y,n}=0$$
for every $n$, using steps 2–3. Under the identification $\mathcal O_E=\varprojlim_n A_n$ in item (4) of [prop-trf-adic-coefficient-morphism-systems], this difference is the tuple all of whose coordinates are zero. Equality of tuples makes it zero. This proves clause (1) for the arbitrary lifts chosen in step 1, and hence for every choice of lifts. The argument also covers $Y_m=\varnothing$, when the sum is zero.

source.place: (1), last sentence: finite sums and equality in the inverse limit

proof.text: In the lattice clause, [lem-trf-lattice-reduction-tower-normalized] makes the quotient reduction tower of $K_{\mathcal O}$ a normalized $A_\bullet$-system, with the canonical associativity maps as its normalization maps. Its finite-Tor constructible levels are assumed in [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model]; item (2) of that proposition supplies the compatible coefficient morphisms $\psi_n=u_n\circ\kappa_{K_n}$. All finite-level witness and admissibility hypotheses remain assumed, so clause (1) applies to this system.

source.place: (2), reduction-tower setup and compatible coefficient morphisms

proof.text: For this reduction tower, the reduction-tower paragraph of [prop-trf-adic-coefficient-morphism-systems] identifies $P_{\mathcal O}$ with $R\Gamma_c(X,K_{\mathcal O})$ and $P_{\bar y,\mathcal O}$ with the completed stalk $K_{\mathcal O,\bar y}$. Use these specified identifications for the following two lift checks.

Item (3) of [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model] says that $U_m$ is the derived limit of the levelwise operators $F_{c,m}(\psi_n)$, so its projections satisfy $\mathrm{pr}_n\circ U_m=F_{c,m}(\psi_n)\circ\mathrm{pr}_n$. Item (2) of [prop-trf-adic-coefficient-morphism-systems] states that an endomorphism with these projection identities is a lift of the compatible family.

source.place: (2), verification that the global operator is a lift

proof.text: For each $y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$, item (4) of [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model] says that $U_{y,m}$ reduces to $\psi_{n,m,\bar y}$. The canonical reduction maps $\pi_n$ in [prop-trf-adic-coefficient-morphism-systems] therefore give $\pi_n\circ(U_{y,m}\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_n)=\psi_{n,m,\bar y}\circ\pi_n$, so $U_{y,m}$ is a lift by item (2) of that proposition. Applying clause (1) to these global and local lifts proves the lattice identity.

source.place: (2), verification that the local operator is a lift and application of (1)

proof_origin.place: Proof (1)–(2), expanded using the statements of the existing DAG nodes
